records.text: Anvilrage Overseers are senior Dark Iron fighters whose magic hastens their own actions. Their title sets them above the rank-and-file Anvilrage, though the evidence gives no individual name or command duties.

Anvilrage Wardens serve among General Angerforge’s forces in Blackrock Depths, where the Kargath Expeditionary Force targets them. They fight with a shield bash and hooked net; summoned wardens can be sent along a waypoint before attacking.

Anvilrage Guardsmen are part of General Angerforge’s forces in Blackrock Depths, targeted by the Kargath Expeditionary Force. They threaten to burn anyone trying to hide and use shield block in combat.
Anvilrage Footmen are among General Angerforge’s first line of forces in Blackrock Depths, targeted by the Kargath Expeditionary Force. In combat, they strike at their opponents.
Anvilrage Soldiers serve among the high-ranking Dark Iron forces in Blackrock Depths, which the Kargath Expeditionary Force has been ordered to destroy. In combat, soldiers use cleave.

Anvilrage Medics serve among the high-ranking Dark Iron forces in Blackrock Depths, targeted by the Kargath Expeditionary Force. Despite their medical role, the supplied combat script has them attack with Mind Blast.
An Anvilrage Officer is a high-ranking Dark Iron official targeted by the Kargath Expeditionary Force in Blackrock Depths. In combat, the officer strikes with a forceful backhand.
A Shadowforge Peasant is a combatant whose fighting includes disarming opponents. Its peasant designation sits alongside a clear ability to defend itself when attacked.
Doomforge Craftsmen are armed combatants who throw wrenches and bombs. When engaged, a craftsman shifts between combat phases and may flee for aid when badly hurt.
An Anvilrage Marshal is a combatant whose fighting style includes a holy strike against opponents.
Doomforge Dragoons are ranged combatants who use Shoot and Explosive Shot in battle.
Doomforge Arcanasmiths fight with Arcane Bolt and use Arcane Explosion against nearby opponents.

An Anvilrage reservist trained for close combat. It opens a fight with a battle shout, then uses shots, Hamstring, and Strike; when badly wounded, it may flee for help. Its routines mark it as a rank-and-file fighter rather than a named leader.
A Shadowforge citizen who can turn dangerous when combat begins, using Cleave. The name places this combatant among the Shadowforge populace, while its behavior is purely martial.
An elite Anvilrage Captain, set apart by the rank attached to its name. The title signals senior standing among Anvilrage fighters.
A Shadowforge Senator who fights with fire and shadow magic, using Fireball and Shadow Bolt. The title gives this figure a civic role.
A Warbringer Construct that cries “Intruders!!” when it draws an attack. Its blunt warning gives it an alarmed, defensive voice, suited to a combat encounter.
A Ragereaver Golem, a combat construct associated with Flurry and a frenzy cue. Its role is that of a direct physical threat, with its visible frenzy signal marking a change in its state.
Wrath Hammer Construct is a combatant that directs Flame Cannon at its victim. That repeated fire attack gives it a clear role in a fight.
Molten War Golem is a combatant that casts Immolate. The fire spell gives this golem a clear flame-based role in an encounter.
Fireguard is a fire-themed combatant that casts Fireball in combat. That attack defines its practical role as a fire attacker.
Blazing Fireguard is a fire combatant that uses both Fire Blast and Immolate in combat. Its two spells distinguish its fighting role from other Fireguards.
Fireguard Destroyer is a combatant that uses Fireball Volley against targets within range. Its area attack gives this heavier Fireguard a ranged role in a fight.
Twilight's Hammer Torturer is a summoned encounter combatant that can use Wracking Pains and Shadow Word: Pain.
A Twilight Emissary who uses Fireball in combat, fighting as a spellcasting opponent.
A Twilight Bodyguard whose fighting style centers on Fist of Ragnaros.
The Twilight's Hammer Ambassador uses curses and elemental shocks in combat, and can strengthen an ally with Bloodlust.
An Arena Spectator that can become involved in combat; when badly hurt, it flees for help.
A Weapon Technician who fights by shooting opponents.
A hound beast whose attacks include Dire Growl and Rend.
A bloodhound mastiff is a beast equipped to detect stealthed intruders and use Expose Weakness and Ravenous Claw in combat.
Panzor the Invincible is a named, rare humanoid.

Moira Bronzebeard is Magni’s daughter, the Princess of Ironforge, and Dagran Thaurissan’s wife. Rescuers are told Dagran controls her. If he is killed during the attempted rescue, she mourns him and condemns the rescuers for leaving her unborn child fatherless. She calls him honorable and demands that Magni be told their Dark Iron child will inherit Ironforge whether he approves or not. Rescuers suspect lingering enchantment, while her responses express grief and determination.
An Ironhand Guardian is a humanoid sentinel.

Golem Lord Argelmach claims the Manufactory and its constructs as his responsibility, warning intruders that they will be destroyed. Lotwil describes him as a dwarf who twisted Lotwil's work for his own purposes, while Marshal Windsor identifies him as one of the villains holding Windsor's lost information.

Cyrus Therepentous describes Bael'Gar as a giant being of pure flame, born of Ragnaros, and seeks the fiery essence within him. Cyrus's request calls for Bael'Gar's defeat and extraction of that essence from his remains.

Lord Incendius declares that Ragnaros's will will bring him back from destruction. Thunderheart believes Incendius is an emissary controlled by a hidden master. Jalinda calls him a purported minion of Ragnaros and fears he will raise Pyron from the ashes again.
High Interrogator Gerstahn is a Twilight's Hammer interrogator.

Emperor Dagran Thaurissan confronts intruders in Blackrock Depths. Ironforge’s rescue account portrays him as an old adversary holding Princess Moira under magical control. He demands aid for the Throne, threatens to crush challengers and dismisses their efforts as futile, boasting that they cannot defeat him.

Commander Gor’shak is an orc of the Kargath Expeditionary Force serving under Thrall. He says he allowed himself to be captured in Blackrock Depths to gather intelligence, then reveals that Princess Moira has been kidnapped by Emperor Thaurissan. He sends an ally to question the dwarf Kharan and report to Thrall, who has a plan to return Moira safely. Gor’shak treats the matter as classified and warns the ally to defend themself when guards approach.

Kharan Mighthammer is a dwarf imprisoned in Blackrock Depths. Magni demands answers from the dwarf who was meant to watch over his missing daughter. Kharan urgently begs for rescue, says Gerstahn has the key, and fears a visitor may intend to kill him. He asks to be heard before judgment, insists he could have done nothing, and sends his account back to Magni.
Dughal Stormwing is a humanoid.

While held prisoner, Marshal Windsor seeks his lost intelligence on the Blackrock menace. He believes General Angerforge and Golem Lord Argelmach hold his information, and asks for help recovering his gear, freeing his friends and escaping.
Pyromancer Loregrain is a fire-focused combatant whose magic includes Flame Shock, Molten Blast, Scorching Totem, and Fire Ward.
Lord Roccor is a combatant whose attacks combine Flame Shock and Earth Shock.
General Angerforge is a Dark Iron commander who coordinated attacks on the 109th division of the K.E.F. and the mass slaughter of its forces. The Horde seeks to bring him to justice.
Hate'rel describes bodily death as a spiritual beginning and speaks of a sacred task shared with others.
Anger'rel identifies as one of the Seven, doomed to stand sentry forever. The words frame that watch as an unending sentence.
Vile'rel names Doom'rel as their leader and presents him as receptive to a challenge.
Gloom'rel offers secrets to those who have paid his price and shown clear intent. He says he has been denied the touch of stone and can never again shape iron.
Seeth'rel bars passage to those who are neither kin nor challengers of the Seven. In combat, this frost wielder uses Frost Armor and Frostbolt.
Doom'rel is bound until challenged; he declares that challengers of the Seven will die. He speaks of the Great Fire and its doom, then confronts the challenger.
Dope'rel calls the Seven's punishment a blessing. In combat, he attacks with Sinister Strike and Rupture.
Fineous Darkvire is the Chief Architect, encountered as an armed opponent in Blackrock Depths. Franclorn Forgewright ties him to Ironfel and the Blackrock Legacy.

Ambassador Flamelash is a hostile, speaking encounter in Blackrock Depths. At the fight's opening he challenges the adventurers, declaring their reign of terror over and calling them to face their doom.
Houndmaster Grebmar is an armed opponent in Blackrock Depths. His title identifies him as a houndmaster, while he uses Demoralizing Shout and Pummel in combat.

Plugger Spazzring tends the tavern's food and drink, promoting his new boar recipe and praising the ale he serves. He tells patrons to drink up and enjoy their drinks, and reacts when he notices suspicious activity or discovers his pockets have been picked.

Mistress Nagmara is a succubus in Blackrock Depths who longs for Private Rocknot, whose charms have not won him over. She seeks ingredients to make a love potion for him, and her dialogue shows her eager, flirtatious manner. In conditional gossip, she later says she and Rocknot are hitting it off; that exchange reflects a relationship development, not a guaranteed outcome for every visitor.
Phalanx says plainly that he does not enjoy conversation.

Private Rocknot is a dwarf in Blackrock Depths whose attention is fixed on Dark Iron Ale. His quest dialogue jokes that sobriety blurs his vision, and his repeated calls for more ale reinforce his thirst. In one exchange, he kisses Mistress Nagmara, linking him to her courtship without establishing what he feels about her.

Hurley Blackbreath is a Dark Iron dwarf tied to the Thunderbrew Lager theft in Blackrock Depths. He guards the stolen ale and reacts angrily when it is threatened, warning intruders away from the kegs and promising they will pay.

Blackbreath Crony is a combatant in Blackrock Depths with a direct connection to Hurley Blackbreath’s stolen Thunderbrew Lager: it can carry the Lost Thunderbrew Recipe sought in the theft investigation.

Ribbly Screwspiggot is a schemer hiding in Blackrock Depths after Baron Revilgaz put a price on his head. His sister describes him as a drain on the family who wastes their money on schemes. When he speaks to a visitor, he offers a plan to make them both rich; if confronted, he panics and calls for help. His gossip can trigger a hostile response.

A patron of the Grim Guzzler who asks Nagmara for Dark Iron ale and mutton and wants more of Plugger’s ale. The patron’s tavern talk supports Ragnaros and the fire elementals, treats Hydraxis’s water elementals as enemies, and ranges from mocking Hydraxis to concern that his recruitment could shift the balance of power.

A tavern patron in Blackrock Depths who asks Nagmara for Dark Iron ale and mutton and wants more of Plugger’s ale. This patron recommends Thunderbrew Lager and drinks before duty. The tavern talk includes a threatening remark about having to restrain an urge to kill a stranger.

A tavern patron in Blackrock Depths who asks Nagmara for Dark Iron ale and mutton. This patron wants to be left alone while partying, challenges people who stare, and mistakes a visitor for serving staff. One remark warns that Plugger may have overfilled a keg until it looks ready to burst.
Ograbisi is a humanoid.
Shill Dinger is a humanoid.
Tobias Seecher is a humanoid.
Crest Killer is a combatant in Blackrock Depths and a direct source of a Dark Iron Fanny Pack, an item Oralius asks adventurers to collect from the Dark Irons in the Depths.
Jaz is a humanoid.

Magmus is an elemental guardian in Emperor Thaurissan’s domain. He warns intruders that the emperor must not be disturbed and threatens them with doom if they persist. He frames his hostility as a duty to protect the emperor and his realm.
A Shadowforge flame keeper in Blackrock Depths who uses a battle shout when drawn into combat.

A crony of Ribbly in Blackrock Depths who wants to be left alone while partying and challenges visitors who stare. This crony orders Dark Iron ale, mistakes a visitor for serving staff, and warns that one of Plugger’s kegs looks overfilled.
An enslaved person in Blackrock Depths.
An undead enslaved figure in Blackrock Depths, identified as having been tortured.

Lokhtos Darkbargainer represents the Thorium Brotherhood in Blackrock Depths, empowered to exchange its favor for Dark Iron ore and cores. He values Dark Iron for Ragnaros’s arms and warns that many Brotherhood members have died seeking fiery cores in the Molten Core. He promotes the Brotherhood’s goods, but can brusquely dismiss visitors as beneath its attention.
Morndeep is an Elder. His seasonal greeting links the new year and bright moon with the awakening of the ancients, and describes the observance as a time to honor the olden races.

Coren Direbrew is a Dark Iron dwarf and the instigator of the Brewfest raids. He resents the surface dwarves' exclusion of Dark Iron brewers from the celebration and insists that his clan's ale is the finest in Azeroth. Defiant and protective of his brew, he treats criticism as an insult and rallies his people to answer it. He wants Dark Iron brewers represented at Brewfest, even as his grievance fuels hostility toward the surface celebration.

A Dark Iron brewer tending two cauldrons of bubbling ale, this brewer worries that Master Coren Direbrew will punish them if the brew is not right. Their work is judged by its taste, and they invite help sampling it while insisting on careful attention to the cauldrons.

Mizli Crankwheel is a busy, blunt worker who insists that everything is under control and has little patience for an unexpected visitor. Mizli asks the visitor to tell Schweitzer and Roitau not to worry, then turns back to work. The exchange shows Mizli coordinating with them, but does not establish what work is underway.

Ognip Blastbolt is occupied with preparations for a show: Ognip tells an unexpected visitor he is busy, says the band plays every night at eight, and remarks to Mizli that they should finish before others arrive. Their exchange shows them working together, though it does not identify the arriving people or guarantee a performance.

place_records.text: You are in Blackrock Depths, a Dark Iron dwarf stronghold beneath Blackrock Mountain. Emperor Dagran Thaurissan rules it, and Golem Lord Argelmach claims its Manufactory. Anvilrage soldiers and bloodhounds fill its halls. Princess Moira Bronzebeard is held captive here by the emperor.
